requirements.requirement: Configure node1, node2, and node3 as a healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster.
requirements.summary: Final checks on all three nodes show MariaDB active and enabled, cluster size 3, a Primary component, connected status, Synced state, and wsrep readiness.

requirements.requirement: Writes submitted through any cluster member are available from the other members.
requirements.summary: Each member accepted a distinct write, and subsequent synchronized reads on every member returned all three writes.

requirements.requirement: The database remains readable and writable with one member unavailable, and that member automatically rejoins with data written during its absence.
requirements.summary: A healthy three-node baseline was observed before node3 was stopped and confirmed unavailable. Node1 and node2 remained a two-member Primary component, served reads, and each committed an outage write. Starting node3 normally caused it to rejoin as Synced and ready with both missed rows; its log directly records receipt of two writesets by IST. Final checks show all three nodes healthy with the same six rows and identical digest.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence: a healthy three-member Galera cluster, multi-primary replication through every member, continued read/write service during a node3 outage, automatic IST recovery, and final data convergence.
limitations: The bounded outage test exercised node3 only; separate disruptions of node1 and node2 were not observed.
The generic after-executor socket inventories were empty and therefore did not independently corroborate the task-specific TCP SQL checks performed shortly beforehand.

operational_hygiene.summary: No executor-caused failed services, package inconsistency, or added /tmp residue was observed. MariaDB finished active and enabled on all nodes, and the temporary package-start policy was explicitly removed.
